parallel.requirements: Recognized the Python argparse plus idna behavior, pure Node.js ESM, .mjs suffixes, local-only imports, no npm dependencies, and matching stdout/newline behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation and assembly ownership while delegating black-box behavioral probing across dimensions through one workflow of child agents.
parallel.implementation: Generated Unicode property data from local tables, wrote pycompat and idna modules under /output/lib, then wrote test8.mjs and patched transitional-warning behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated generated data, IDNA checks, codec, argparse, repr, and entrypoint into /output; status artifact validation lists test8.mjs and the module tree.
parallel.verification: Used local oracle probes, child-provided specs, sample runs, and official evaluation; a child had to reverify argparse cases after shared temporary-output contamination.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with some children still in progress or retrying, the agent process timed out, and the current official result remains 19/20 rather than pass.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Python argparse and idna behavior plus the ESM, .mjs, local import, no dependency, and exact output constraints.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one agent without workflow or child delegation, sequentially probing behavior, writing libraries, fixing bugs, and setting up differential tests.
serial.implementation: Built a separate pure ESM IDNA port with modules such as punycodec, core, pyio, argparse, pyrepr, unicodeprops, bidi, and test8.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Assembled the serial module tree and entrypoint in /output; status artifact validation lists test8.mjs and the expected library files.
serial.verification: Ran the four sample cases after fixing a punycode hang and created a broad differential corpus, but the run timed out before a complete pass was achieved.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process also timed out and the current official evaluation is 19/20, so one hidden testcase remained failing despite no delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the need for a Node.js ESM, .mjs, no-npm black-box port matching argparse and IDNA stdout behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and requirements, including exact command-line parsing and pure local ESM modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference is evidenced; both attempted the same broad IDNA/argparse contract and both failed one testcase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split behavioral discovery into workflow children while the parent owned implementation and final artifact assembly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows and agent tools disabled and kept all probing, implementation, and verification in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main structural difference is delegated probing versus single-agent execution, not a different owner for the final implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts included shared known facts and dimension-specific probe tasks, returning structured behavioral specs when completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probe findings in one context and converted them directly into modules and tests without child handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff surfaces through structured child results, but no missing or conflicting interface contract is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel generated local Unicode data, wrote layered pycompat/unicode/idna modules, wrote argparse, and created test8.mjs before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote its own layered modules and entrypoint, including a punycodec fix after a hang and broad differential corpus creation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both built full local ESM IDNA ports, but with different module layouts and independent implementation details; both achieved the same official 19/20.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflow state shows completed child results mixed with in-progress or retried children and a killed aggregate workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child workflow lifecycle; its results were local tool outputs in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-result lifecycle complexity and an aborted workflow, while serial had no delegated result retrieval problem.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probe children shared the same sandbox and at least two detected or recorded contamination of shared /tmp probe outputs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, so temporary files were produced and consumed by the same serial actor rather than concurrently shared children.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The retained process difference is shared temporary-artifact contamination in parallel; serial had no equivalent multi-actor shared artifact boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used local sample probes and official evaluation; contaminated probe evidence required re-verification before being reliable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample cases after a punycode fix and created a differential corpus, then official evaluation also reported 19/20.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had substantial but incomplete verification; only parallel had a demonstrated need to redo contaminated probe evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a workflow with 14 child logs, nearly the full 2400-second budget, and ended with process returncode 143.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also consumed nearly the full budget and ended with process returncode 143, but without child token or workflow overhead.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out and both failed one testcase; the timeout is shared, while parallel added child workflow overhead and a killed workflow state.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are concordant: parallel and serial both have solution_passed false with 19/20 passed samples. The process difference is delegated parallel probing versus a serial one-agent port, and the concrete parallel-only adverse episode is shared temporary probe artifact contamination. That episode explains a process hazard and rework boundary, not an official outcome difference, because the serial control also failed one testcase.
parallel_contributors: Workflow-based probing produced shared temporary-file contamination that had to be reverified.
The workflow was killed with some probe/critique children still in progress while the parent timed out after final edits.
serial_contributors: The serial run avoided child-workflow shared state and built a comparable local ESM IDNA port in one trajectory.
The serial run still timed out and failed one official testcase, showing the remaining failure is not uniquely explained by parallel coordination.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two ports used different module structures and independent Unicode/IDNA implementations.
Both final artifacts were accepted for evaluation and both passed 19 of 20 samples.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a directly evidenced adverse parallel process consequence only

candidates.reason: The parallel parent retained implementation ownership: it generated data, wrote the IDNA modules, and wrote the entrypoint; children were probe/spec workers.
Integration was not ownerless: the parent assembled generated tables, runtime modules, and entrypoint edits into the delivered artifact.
The required entrypoint and library tree were assembled in /output and artifact validation found the expected test8.mjs file.
The parent owned the end-to-end pipeline from probing through code generation and sample checks; timeout is not an absent pipeline owner.
Productive implementation was not blocked behind one serial preflight; the parent built Unicode data and modules while the workflow probes ran.
Although there was heavy probing, implementation overlapped with investigation and was not deferred until a separate completed investigation phase.
The indispensable implementation path had an active parent owner and a delivered artifact; no specific required task was shown starved by auxiliary child work.
The workflow had many children and was killed, but no independent required deliverable failure is tied to collective fan-out beyond the separately retained temp-artifact contamination.
No single child owned an overbroad indispensable implementation assignment whose unfinished scope left the final deliverable incomplete.

The executed child briefs carried the executable path, source-reading instruction, no-python rule, known observations, and specific probe dimensions; no known omitted requirement made child work unusable.
Children produced behavioral specifications rather than separately owned implementation components, so no omitted cross-agent API/file contract caused incompatible code.
No known finding is shown present before transfer and omitted after transfer in a way that caused repeated work or a wrong implementation step.
Child handoffs were large, but completed structured findings were available and used as specifications; volume alone did not leave a required action materially unconsumed.
No receiver is shown acting on a superseded child report or stale workspace fact that caused rework or invalid verification.
No incompatible child reports or contracts remained unadjudicated at a parent decision point; local re-probing resolved uncertainty.
The parent did not make a non-evaluator whole-task acceptance decision despite a visible integrated gap; the run timed out and the official evaluator later reported 19/20.
Workflow retries occurred after stalls, but the retry prompts included prior common facts and there is no observed no-checkpoint repetition that caused the needed output to fail.

candidates.reason: The workflow was killed with children in progress, but the interrupted children were support probes, not an active required implementation result proven necessary and finalized too early.
There was no complete unpromoted candidate waiting for final placement; the parent wrote the entrypoint and artifact validation copied the output tree.
No child implementation was merged after relevant integrated verification without a post-merge check; child work was behavioral evidence, not code merged after tests.
No delegated implementation completed and then remained unjoined; implementation was written by the parent rather than by child implementers.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent; incomplete workflow children did not provide a returned verifier result needed at closure.
Stalled or killed probe children did not own required implementation scope, and the parent continued local probing and implementation rather than leaving a failed child scope ownerless.
Completed child results existed in workflow state, but no parent-visible returned result is shown being ignored in a way inconsistent with the final implementation.
The parent did not merely wait for timeout; it continued active data generation, code writing, and final edits while the workflow ran.
Concurrent agents did not write competing implementation files or behavior-owning modules that required reconciliation.
The observed shared path issue involved temporary probe output, not two live agents editing the same source or configuration file.
No non-entry library/module/configuration source produced or actively owned by another agent was replaced or deleted.
No child owned or used the required entrypoint or submitted artifact while another actor replaced it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion overwrote multiple current final outputs or invalidated another final-tree owner.
The live conflict was in shared temporary probe files, not a shared implementation workspace causing source-tree provenance instability.

A parallel child detected that other actors shared /tmp during probing, and another child documented that shared /tmp/o had contaminated argparse evidence before re-verification with unique mktemp files.
candidates.realized_consequence: Probe evidence became contaminated by another concurrent actor through shared temporary output files and had to be discarded or re-run with isolated temp paths.
candidates.near_match_reason: The contaminated object was temporary probe output, not implementation workspace source or final-tree state.

retained_patterns.reason: Parallel child probes used shared temporary output paths; one child identified the /tmp race and another documented contaminated argparse evidence reverified with per-invocation mktemp files.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: A concurrent actor polluted temporary probe output, making at least one child probe result untrustworthy until re-run with isolated temp files.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The concrete adverse state was temporary probe artifact leakage, not concurrent implementation workspace writes or source-tree provenance loss.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Workflow killed and stalled-child symptoms were treated as one downstream lifecycle/budget chain and rejected because no separate required implementation consequence was proven.
Concurrent write labels were rejected because the proven same-path problem affected temporary probe outputs, making Artifact Leakage the more specific label.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the shared /tmp contamination episode clears the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No timeout, retry, handoff, or write-collision label is duplicated around the same episode; the retained pattern has unique anchors and consequence.
